Action.description: The action proposed for a candidate.

oneOf.description: No action: the item is blocked (S3) or inspect-only.
Delete through the safe executor (S0 default, D-3). Restore path is regeneration.
Atomic same-volume move into `.scull-quarantine/<operation-id>/` (S1/S2 default).
Move to the platform Trash / Recycle Bin (fallback when quarantine isn't possible).
Run a tool's own cleanup command (package caches, Docker; SAFE-06, QC-03).
`git worktree remove` (never `--force` unless authorized per item).
`git worktree prune` for a stale registration.

Activity.description:
The newest modification observed inside a worktree.

Missing evidence never counts as evidence of inactivity (PRD §8.4): when the sample is
incomplete, the true newest modification may be later than [`Activity::newest_unix`].

complete.description:
Whether every entry was looked at. `false` when the bound was hit or some folder or entry
couldn't be read: the newest modification is then a lower bound.

newest_unix.description: Unix timestamp (seconds, UTC) of the newest modification time seen, if any entry had one.

ArtifactCleanup.description:
Whether the worktree's regenerable artifacts may be cleaned on their own (GIT-03, last
column). Each artifact is still classified by the PRD §8.3 rubric.

oneOf.description: Allowed.
The worktree is in use: blocked for this run.
The worktree folder is missing: nothing to clean.

Candidate.description:
A detected item with a risk tier and evidence. This is the unit the preview shows, plans
reference and the executor revalidates.

artifact.description: Human-readable artifact type, e.g. "Cargo build output".

identity.description: File identity at scan time; revalidation compares against it (SAFE-05).

tier.description: Tier: always the most protective of `reasons` (see [`Candidate::is_consistent`]).

Category.description: Broad category of a candidate, used for grouping in the CLI, charts and Quick Clean.

oneOf.description: Build output or dependencies inside a project (`target/`, `node_modules`, `.next`, …).
Global package-manager cache (Quick Clean, QC-01).
A Git worktree, whole or stale registration.
ML/AI model or dataset cache.
Docker / container data.
Large file surfaced for inspection only.
scull's own data (database, logs, quarantine; DATA-05).
Anything else.

CommitList.description: Commits reachable from HEAD but from no remote-tracking ref.

Confidence.description: How confident the engine is in a reclaim estimate (PRD §9).

oneOf.description: No sharing, snapshots or clones could affect the result.
Minor uncertainty (e.g. compression we measured but can't fully attribute).
Shared extents, clones or snapshots may pin some bytes.
The engine can't estimate; only the measured delta will tell.

ConfigWarning.description: A non-fatal configuration problem: the setting was ignored, scanning continues.

ConfigWarningCode.description: Why a configuration setting was ignored.

oneOf.description: The repository file is not valid TOML; its directory was protected instead.
A setting repository files may not change (roots, rules, MCP, forge, output, threads).
A setting that would lower protection (an S0 tier, a shorter activity window).
A path that is absolute, uses `..`, a drive letter, a UNC prefix or `~`.
A value of the wrong type or format.
A key scull doesn't know.

Evidence.description:
A fact observed about a candidate. Evidence is what the preview shows under "why".

Missing evidence never counts as evidence of inactivity (PRD §8.4): when a signal can't be
read, record [`Evidence::SignalUnavailable`] instead of omitting it.

oneOf.description:
A project marker at the expected relative location (e.g. `Cargo.toml` beside `target/`).
CLS-03: a directory name alone is never enough.
A lockfile or manifest the artifact can be reproduced from.
The artifact type is known to a rule.

artifact.description: Human-readable artifact type, e.g. "Cargo build output".

oneOf.description: Files inside the candidate are tracked by Git.

files.description: Number of tracked files found (may be a lower bound).

oneOf.description: The path is inside a protected root (SAFE-03).
The user excluded this path in config.
A `.scull-protect` marker covers this path.
The candidate is in use right now.

by.description: Process name or tool, if known.

signal.description: What showed it, e.g. "open handle", "process cwd", "cargo lock".

oneOf.description: Newest modification inside the candidate, sampled with a bound.

newest_unix.description: Unix timestamp (seconds, UTC) of the newest observed mtime.

sampled.description: Whether sampling hit its bound (the true newest may be later).

oneOf.description: The candidate crosses a mount or volume boundary.
Reached through a symlink or junction pointing outside the scan root.
Cloud-sync placeholder or synced folder (iCloud, OneDrive, Dropbox). Never hydrated.
Hardlinks shared with something outside the candidate (e.g. pnpm store).
A signal could not be read on this platform or with current permissions.
Free-form note from a detector (shown, never used for tiering).

FileIdentity.description: Path-independent identity of a filesystem object (device/volume + inode/file ID).

file.description: Inode / file ID as lowercase hex.

Flags.description:
Risk flags shown with every candidate (SAFE-01). `None` means "not checked / unknown",
which is never treated as "no".

active.description: In use by a process or tool.

cloud_placeholder.description: Is or contains a cloud-sync placeholder.

hardlinked.description: Contains hardlinks shared outside the candidate.

FsPath.description:
A filesystem path as it appears in plans, JSON output and the database.

Serialized as a string. Paths that aren't valid Unicode (possible on Unix and Windows) are
converted lossily with U+FFFD and flagged by [`FsPath::is_lossy`]; the engine never acts on
a path read back from JSON alone. Items are matched by [`crate::ItemId`] and file identity,
and candidates are re-derived from the disk before execution (SAFE-05, SAFE-11).

oneOf.description: A branch is checked out.

oid.description: The commit it points at; `None` for an unborn branch (no commits yet).

oneOf.description: HEAD is detached.

HistoryOutcome.description: Whether the scan was recorded in history.

oneOf.description: History is off for this run (`--no-history`, or no database).
Recorded.

disappeared.description: Items marked gone by this scan (only after a completed scan).

new_items.description: Items seen for the first time.

oneOf.description: Recording failed; the scan result is still valid.

Issue.description: Something the scan could not read or did not descend into.

oneOf.description: Permission denied.
Vanished while scanning.
Listing took too long.
Another read error.
On another volume: counted, not descended.
A directory loop: not descended.
Depth limit: not descended.
A Git operation failed.
Something outside the scan roots that was not measured.
History could not be recorded.

ItemId.description: Stable item ID: 128-bit truncated SHA-256 of identity + path, lowercase hex.

LockState.description: Lock state of a linked worktree.

oneOf.description: Not locked.
Locked with `git worktree lock`; must be shown with its reason (FX-GIT-09).

reason.description: The reason given with `--reason`, if any.

MatchedArtifact.description: An ignored entry that a detector rule recognised as a regenerable artifact.

path.description: The entry, relative to the worktree.

MergeStatus.description: Whether HEAD is merged, and **how that was determined** (GIT-02).

oneOf.description: Proven: HEAD is an ancestor of a default-branch ref.
Proven pushed: HEAD is reachable from a remote-tracking ref (so every commit on it is).

refs.description:
Some of the remote-tracking refs that contain HEAD (may be empty if listing them
failed after reachability was established).

oneOf.description:
Heuristic only: every commit on HEAD missing from the default branch has a
patch-equivalent commit there (`git cherry` / patch-id), as after a squash or rebase
merge. Not proof (GIT-03: S2 "merge unproven").
The branch has no commits (unborn): nothing can be lost.
No proof and no heuristic match against any default-branch ref.
Couldn't be determined (Git error, no default branch found, HEAD unknown).

Observed.description: A fact that may not have been observable. `Unknown` is never treated as the safe answer.

oneOf.description: The fact was observed.
The fact could not be observed.

Observed2.description: A fact that may not have been observable. `Unknown` is never treated as the safe answer.

oneOf.description: The fact was observed.
The fact could not be observed.

Observed3.description: A fact that may not have been observable. `Unknown` is never treated as the safe answer.

oneOf.description: The fact was observed.
The fact could not be observed.

Observed4.description: A fact that may not have been observable. `Unknown` is never treated as the safe answer.

oneOf.description: The fact was observed.
The fact could not be observed.

Observed5.description: A fact that may not have been observable. `Unknown` is never treated as the safe answer.

oneOf.description: The fact was observed.
The fact could not be observed.

Observed6.description: A fact that may not have been observable. `Unknown` is never treated as the safe answer.

oneOf.description: The fact was observed.
The fact could not be observed.

Observed7.description: A fact that may not have been observable. `Unknown` is never treated as the safe answer.

oneOf.description: The fact was observed.
The fact could not be observed.

Observed8.description: A fact that may not have been observable. `Unknown` is never treated as the safe answer.

oneOf.description: The fact was observed.
The fact could not be observed.

ParentRepo.description: The repository a worktree belongs to.

common_dir.description: The common Git dir (identifies the repository).

main_worktree.description: The main working tree, for a non-bare repository.

PathList.description: A list of worktree-relative paths, capped for display.

paths.description:
The paths (`/`-separated, relative to the worktree; a trailing `/` marks a whole folder
Git collapsed into one entry). At most [`AnalyzeOptions::max_paths`].

total.description: How many entries Git reported in total.

oneOf.description: A required metadata file (`gitdir`, `commondir`) is missing.
A metadata file has unexpected contents, is not a regular file, or is too large.
A metadata file or the worktree's `.git` file could not be read.
`commondir` resolves to a different repository than the one it is registered in.

The claimed worktree's `.git` does not point back to this admin dir (moved, copied,
or crafted). The folder is *not* treated as a worktree of this repository.

ProjectRef.description: The project or repository that owns a candidate.

name.description: Display name (usually the directory name or manifest name).

ProjectSummary.description:
A project: a directory with a project marker (`Cargo.toml`, `package.json`, ...) or the
owner of a detected artifact.

allocated.description: Allocated bytes of those candidates per tier.

badge.description:
Most protective tier among its candidates (parent badge, PRD §8.3); `null` without
candidates.

candidates.description: Candidates attributed to this project (by their first project).

git_worktree.description: The Git worktree the project lives in, if any.

markers.description: Marker files found in the directory.

newest_mtime.description: Newest modification time seen in the project (Unix seconds), when measured.

reclaimable.description: Reclaimable bytes of those candidates per tier.

total_allocated.description: Allocated size of the whole project directory, when measured.

Reachability.description: Whether HEAD's commit is reachable from any ref.

oneOf.description: Reachable from these refs (a branch HEAD is reachable from its branch).
Reachable from no ref: only the worktree's detached HEAD keeps it (FX-GIT-07).
HEAD has no commit (unborn branch).

ReasonCode.description:
Stable codes for tier reasons. Matches the rows of the rubric (PRD §8.3) and the worktree
decision table (GIT-03). New codes may be added; existing ones never change meaning.

oneOf.description: Contains Git-tracked files → S3.
Inside a protected root → S3.
Matches a user exclusion → S3.
Covered by `.scull-protect` → S3.
In use (open handles, process cwd, held lock) → S3 for this run.
Crosses a mount/volume boundary → S3.
Reached via a link outside the scan root → S3.
Cloud placeholder or synced folder → S2.
Marker found but nothing to reproduce from → S2.
Modified within the activity window → one tier more protective.
A required signal was unavailable, so the engine assumed the protective answer.
Reproducible, but needs network or a long build → S1.
Reproducible from local inputs or quickly → S0.
Worktree is locked → S3.
Worktree has uncommitted or untracked changes → S3.
Worktree has ignored files not matched by an artifact rule → ≥ S2.
Commits not reachable from any remote-tracking ref and not provably merged → S3.
Detached HEAD at a commit reachable from no ref → S3.
Merge detected only heuristically → S2.
Clean, unlocked, everything pushed or merged → S1 (never S0).
Registered worktree whose directory is gone → S0 (metadata only).
Package cache: re-downloadable → S1 (QC-02).
Large file surfaced for inspection only → S2.

Reclaimable.description: Physically reclaimable bytes plus the confidence of that estimate.

bytes.description: Estimated bytes freed. With `Confidence::Unknown` this is a best guess, not a promise.

shared_bytes.description:
Bytes shared with something else (e.g. hardlinked into the pnpm store) that removing
this item will not free while the other links remain.

Regeneration.description:
How to get an item back after removal, and roughly what it costs (D-5: "unknown" unless
there is evidence).

RegenerationCost.description: Estimated cost of regenerating an item.

oneOf.description: No evidence to estimate from (default, D-5).
An estimate backed by evidence.
Cannot be regenerated (unique data).

RepoConfigWarning.description: A repository-file setting that was ignored (CFG-03).

RuleRef.description: Reference to the detector rule that produced a candidate (CLS-01).

version.description: Rule version; bumps whenever the rule's matching or tiering changes.

ScanSummary.description: The `summary` record: the [`ScanReport`] without its candidate list.

cancelled.description: Whether the user cancelled (the report is partial).

candidate_count.description: Number of `candidate` lines written before this one.

finished_at.description: Unix time (seconds) the scan finished or was cancelled.

issues.description: Places that could not be read or were not descended.

signals_unavailable.description: Signals that could not be observed.

worktree_problems.description: Worktree registrations that could not be trusted.

SignalUnavailable.description: A safety signal the run could not observe.

reason.description: Why, and what scull did instead.

Sizes.description: The three size figures for an item.

allocated.description: Blocks actually allocated on disk (accounts for sparse files and compression).

reclaimable.description: Estimated free-space increase if the item were removed now.

dirty.description: Whether its work tree (or a nested submodule's) has tracked changes or untracked files.

initialized.description: Whether it is checked out (has a `.git`). An uninitialized submodule has no local files.

Tier.description:
How much risk removing an item carries.

The ordering is by **protectiveness**: `S0 < S1 < S2 < S3`. Combining evidence always takes
the maximum (the most protective tier), and a tier may only ever move *up* this order after a
scan (invariant I-8: tiers never decrease on revalidation).

oneOf.description:
Regenerable: a verified generated artifact, reproducible from tracked inputs.
Preselected for review, but never executed without confirmation.
Costly to recreate: reproducible, but needs a significant download or build. Opt-in.
Uncertain: ownership, activity or reproducibility is unclear. Never preselected.
Protected: possibly unique data, in active use, or explicitly protected. Never acted on.

TierBreakdown.description:
Bytes per tier, used to aggregate parent nodes for charts (PRD §8.3 "Aggregation").

A parent's *badge* is the most protective tier that has any bytes; charts must never color a
parent as safe when it contains S2/S3 bytes.

TierReason.description:
Why a candidate got (at least) a given tier. One per rubric row that fired (PRD §8.3); the
candidate's tier is the most protective of these.

message.description: Short human explanation shown in the preview.

tier.description: The minimum tier this reason imposes.

Totals.description:
Byte totals over a set of candidates, split by tier (PHY-01: every size is labeled).

Linked worktrees are totalled separately (`worktrees`), since their bytes include the
artifacts inside them.

count.description: Number of candidates per tier (artifacts and caches).

Upstream.description: The configured upstream of the checked-out branch.

ahead.description: Commits on HEAD not on the upstream, when known.

behind.description: Commits on the upstream not on HEAD, when known.

exists.description:
Whether the upstream ref exists locally (it is gone after the remote branch was deleted
and pruned).

action.description:
The whole-worktree action: [`Action::GitWorktreePrune`] for a stale registration (S0),
[`Action::GitWorktreeRemove`] (never `--force`) at S1, [`Action::Quarantine`] at S2,
[`Action::None`] at S3. Never deletes a branch.

artifacts.description: Ignored entries recognised as regenerable artifacts.

evidence.description: Facts to show under "why" (activity, unavailable signals, in-use).

unique_ignored.description: Ignored entries no artifact rule matched, by name (the preview must list them).

WorktreeKind.description: The role of a worktree in its repository.

oneOf.description: The main working tree of a non-bare repository.
The entry for a bare repository itself (no working tree).
A linked worktree created with `git worktree add`.

WorktreeProblem.description: A linked-worktree registration that could not be trusted.

claimed_path.description: The worktree folder it claims, when that much could be read.

WorktreeProblemReport.description: A worktree registration that could not be trusted.

WorktreeReport.description: One worktree with its GIT-02 state and GIT-03 decision.

allocated.description: Allocated size of the folder, when measured.

candidate.description: Item ID of its candidate, when it is one.

inside_roots.description:
Whether the folder lies inside a scan root. Worktrees elsewhere are reported but never
offered as candidates.

path.description: The worktree folder (for a stale registration, the folder it was registered at).

WorktreeState.description: Everything GIT-02 reports about one worktree. Serializable for `--json` output.

activity.description:
Last observed activity (supplied by the caller, see [`sample_activity`]).

[`sample_activity`]: crate::sample_activity

head_reachability.description: Whether HEAD's commit is reachable from any ref (FX-GIT-07, -08).

ignored.description:
Ignored paths, by name (FX-GIT-04). Folders Git ignores as a whole appear once, as
`dir/`.

merge.description: Merge status and how it was determined (FX-GIT-01, -06).

missing.description:
The worktree folder no longer exists: a stale registration that `git worktree prune`
would remove (metadata only, FX-GIT-10). Nothing else was analysed.

submodules.description: Submodules and whether their work trees have local changes (FX-GIT-13).

tracked_changes.description:
Tracked paths with staged or unstaged changes, including conflicts and changed
submodule commits (FX-GIT-02).

unpushed.description: Commits not reachable from any remote-tracking ref (FX-GIT-05, -11, -12).

upstream.description: Upstream of the checked-out branch (`None` when detached or not configured).

count.description: Number of worktree candidates per tier.

description: One line of `--ndjson` output with schema scull/scan@1: `type` selects the shape of `data`.

oneOf.description: A candidate (one line each, most reclaimable first).
The last line: everything else in the report.

version.description: The scull version that wrote it.
